estimator_concordance.interpretation: Two estimators applied within the same published notebook and folded-product context agree on an offset of about five percent of a cycle. This is internal method concordance, not an independent-data replication.

TOPA_interpretation: The radio and X-ray behavior is consistent with a common approximately 44-minute clock, but the published notebook does not support treating the peaks as exactly zero-phase coincident.
The measured relative offset is approximately 0.05 cycle, corresponding to roughly 135-146 seconds for the public timing period.
The two estimator uncertainties overlap and their central estimates differ by only about 11.5 seconds, strengthening the case that the offset is not merely one estimator's numerical artifact.
Because both estimators use the same underlying folded products, their agreement does not satisfy TOPA's independence gate.
The lag sign convention is preserved exactly as reported; no physical statement about which band leads is promoted until the notebook convention and time-axis definition are independently verified.
This gate promotes common periodic physical behavior and a measurable relative phase structure. It does not identify the emitting object or mechanism.
